newsitem.title: UK: Europe retailers want US gene crops identified.
newsitem.headline: Europe retailers want US gene crops identified.

text.p: European retailers have urged U.S. agribusiness companies to make sure that genetically modified crops of maize and soya can be identified.

"U.S. commodity agribusiness, from seed developer to farmer and elevator business, need to act rapidly and introduce streamed handling so commodity buyers can guarantee manufacturers and therefore consumers the actual provenance of the soya and maize," a group of European retail trade organisations and individual retailers said in an open letter to U.S. suppliers.
"Consumer acceptance of biotechnology in Europe stands at what is likely to be a decisive crossroads," it said.
"It is important that U.S. agribusiness understand this," the group said. "Otherwise, the 1996 U.S. harvest of genetically modified soya and maize could be the last to be welcomed in Europe,"

"(European) retailers have for a long time asked US agribusiness to provide traceability and this has not been forthcoming," a spokesman for the British Retail Consortium, the UK retailers organisation, which sent out the letter on behalf of the sector in Europe, told Reuters.
"It's that which has led to this initiative," he said.

"The inability, or is it the unwillingness, of U.S. agribusiness to innovate in its collection and distribution systems, in order to address the simple lack of in-built traceability from field to elevator and on to European shores, threatens the cause of biotechnology and its huge potential for good," the letter said.
"We hope that this message, on behalf of our customers is clear. Work with us, to ensure open and transparent systems that deliver choice," it said.
"In the longer term it will be to everyone's benefit, not least of all to those most intimately involved in the development of GM (genetically modified) technologies and foodstuffs," It said.

The letter is signed by representatives of trade groups in Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Sweden and the UK, as well as a range of leading European food retailers including Britain's Sainsbury and Tesco.
